A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. All 30 pages of each version, including equations, tables, figures and appendices, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original mesh parameterization experiments, ablations, runtime measurements and a 115-participant user study in Section 4 and Appendix A.3.

after.justification: v3 retains the original mesh experiments, ablations, runtime measurements and user-study outcomes, including Tables 1–10.

M1.justification: The four-network backbone, ShDF partitioning, per-part parameterization and packing, and AO-weighted seam optimization remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 has an edited title and comment but retains the same computational steps.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same semantic and visibility tasks, simple and complex meshes, packing scenarios, and expert and general user populations. Appendix examples are retained under revised figure numbers.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain FlexPara, OptCuts, xatlas, Blender and Maya. The SAMesh/PartField partitioning comparisons and Maya/Blender/Houdini packing comparisons also remain unchanged; removing repeated citations does not remove comparators.

E3.justification: The study still includes 45 experts and 70 general participants, each completing five semantic and six visibility comparisons. SAMesh reference labels, evaluation metrics and reported experimental settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: Partitioning, packing, visibility-loss, geometry-tradeoff and runtime analyses are retained. Removed v2 Figure 6 repeats the Duckie AO distributions already shown in v2 Figure 8, retained as v3 Figure 7; the accompanying with/without-loss discussion also remains.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same point estimates, preference percentages and AO distributions. Neither introduces repeated-run or seed information, confidence intervals, error bars or significance testing.

E6.justification: Tables 1–10 retain their numerical entries, including the proposed visibility pipeline's seam AO of 0.6065 in Table 1 and semantic pipeline's Hamming distance of 0.3188 in Table 3. Matched qualitative panels and plotted distributions are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–19 retain the same definitions, graph-cut energy, mapping constructions, seam approximation and loss formulations. No mathematical assumption, derivation or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about semantic alignment, visibility-guided seams, geometry-preserving learning and improved texture usability.

C2.justification: The Section 3 overview drops its characterization of the entire two-stage framework as 'end-to-end differentiable,' modestly qualifying the mechanism description without changing the procedure. Interpretations of distortion tradeoffs, segmentation limitations and computational bottlenecks otherwise remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 adds a project-page pointer on the first page while retaining the existing implementation-code link. Architecture specifications, ShDF defaults, implementation libraries and computational details remain unchanged; the new pointer does not establish newly available code.

R1.justification: The reference list and substantive positioning relative to prior UV parameterization and perceptual approaches are unchanged. In-text citations are standardized and some repeated citations removed, without adding or removing cited works overall.

P1.justification: v3 adds the conference-publication header and acknowledgments, tightens several captions and prose passages, and edits Algorithm 1's wording. The LLM-use statement is consolidated on page 22; the overall section organization remains stable.

P2.justification: v3 removes the redundant main-text Figure 6, renumbers subsequent figures, enlarges appendix Tables 6–10 and adjusts float placement and captions. Retained figure imagery and table contents are unchanged.

improvement.justification: Larger appendix tables and tighter captions improve readability, while the project-page pointer improves resource navigation. Readers now consult appendix Figure 7 for the AO histograms formerly duplicated in the main text, but the evidence is preserved. These are modest quality gains; the methods, experimental support and main conclusions remain unchanged.
